title: Lost GET — Reporting and Recovery
body: A missing tooth, adapter, or shroud that gets loaded, hauled, and dumped into the crusher turns into a liner strike — major plant downtime and a real injury risk from a rock-out or jammed liner repair. Every hour spent chasing a GET piece through the crusher costs far more than the five minutes it takes to stop and search for it at the face.
keyPoints: Stop first, every time. The moment GET loss is suspected, the operator halts — don't keep digging while a piece is unaccounted for.
Report with specifics: equipment ID, operator, time, GPS location, and exactly what's missing — that's what lets Survey and the search crew actually find it.
Recovery is controlled, not frantic — visual search, GPS-pinpointed excavation, and tracking the material's path to pit, stockpile, ROM pad, or crusher if it isn't found right away.

If it's not recovered on the spot, the chain doesn't stop — surveyors mark the area after the next blast, the excavator operator keeps watching that position, and the ROM pad loader operator is the last line of defense before the primary crusher.
Prevention beats recovery — pre-start and daily GET checks, and operators trained to recognize the feel and sound of a lost tooth before it's gone.
apply: At the loading face, if an excavator operator reports a rough dig or an odd sound on the bucket, don't wave it off as normal wear — treat it as a possible GET loss and get it checked before that bucket load moves anywhere near the crusher feed.
